title: Matching q-prime coefficient frame
statement: For the normalized second quotient map q-prime specified by the pullback-composition comparison, and the same local data satisfying the q formula, there is a second frame section giving the q-prime formula with the same coefficients. This does not assert a formula for arbitrary module morphisms.

source.place: Tags 01N2, 01NQ, 01NR and 01OB, split into the first and second normalized chart equations.

proof.text: Use the normalized degree-one fraction formulas for D and D-prime on corresponding standard opens. The generator equation hb identifies the coefficients, hence the kernels of the two normalized quotient maps on generators. The pulled affine sections generate the source locally. The q formula and surjectivity show that a is a frame and its coefficients generate the unit ideal locally. The second quotient therefore gives a unique matching section b-prime locally. The coefficient equations force these sections to agree on overlaps; sheaf gluing gives b-prime on the given Z. No claim for an arbitrary q-prime is used.

proof_origin.place: Tags 01N2, 01NQ, 01NR, 01OB: normalized quotient compatibility, with local frame and sheaf gluing.

lean.statement:
theorem normalized_pullback_generator_local_coefficients_qprime
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ S) (E : S.Modules) [E.IsQuasicoherent]
    [((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback g).obj E).IsQuasicoherent]
    (D : ProjectiveBundleQuotientGeometry.TautologicalQuotient E)
    (D' : ProjectiveBundleQuotientGeometry.TautologicalQuotient
      ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback g).obj E))
    (b : Scheme.GradedAlgebraData.PullbackData g (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E)
      (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback g).obj E)))
    (hb : ∀ (U : S.affineOpens) (W : X.affineOpens) (h : W.1 ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)
      (m : E.val.obj (op U.1)),
      b.map h (SymmetricAlgebra.ι Γ(S, U.1) _ m) =
        SymmetricAlgebra.ι Γ(X, W.1) _
          (((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback g).obj E).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op
            (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackSection g E U.1 m)))
    (e : (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback
        (b.relProjComparison ≫ (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom)).obj E =
      (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback
        ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData
          ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback g).obj E)).relProjHom ≫ g)).obj E) :
    let T := (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData
      ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback g).obj E)).relProj
    let M := (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback
      (b.relProjComparison ≫ (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom)).obj E
    let P := (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback b.relProjComparison).obj D.line
    let q : M ⟶ P :=
      (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackSectionComp b.relProjComparison
        (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom).hom.app E ≫
        (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback b.relProjComparison).map D.quotient
    let q' : M ⟶ D'.line := (eqToIso e).hom ≫
      (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackSectionComp
        (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData
          ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback g).obj E)).relProjHom g).hom.app E ≫ D'.quotient
    ∀ (U : S.affineOpens) (W : T.Opens) (h : W ≤
      (b.relProjComparison ≫ (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom) ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)
      (x : T) (Z : T.Opens) (hZW : Z ≤ W) (hx : x ∈ Z)
      (a : Γ(P, Z)) (c : Γ(E, U.1) → Γ(T, Z)),
      (∀ t : Γ(E, U.1),
        let s := M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (hZW.trans h)).op
          (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackSection
            (b.relProjComparison ≫ (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom)
            E U.1 t)
        q.app Z s = c t • a) →
      ∃ (b' : Γ(D'.line, Z)),
        ∀ t : Γ(E, U.1),
          let s := M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (hZW.trans h)).op
            (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackSection
              (b.relProjComparison ≫ (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom)
              E U.1 t)
          q'.app Z s = c t • b'

statement_change.old_statement: For the same local data satisfying the q formula, there is a second frame section giving the q-prime formula.
statement_change.what: The Lean declaration quantified over an arbitrary q-prime, although the source and parent require the normalized pulled quotient. For E = k^2 on P^1, on the chart q = (1,t), the arbitrary map q-prime = (0,1) cannot have the same coefficients (1,t): the first basis vector forces b-prime = 0, the second forces 1 = 0. Replace the arbitrary-map binder by the normalized quotient of the parent.
